title: The bag by the door
label: PACKED FOR WEEKS. STILL HERE.
lead: Hook 1, because the object-truth shape lands the conflict in one breath and everyone who owns a gym bag has seen this exact one.

hooks.label: PACKED FOR WEEKS. STILL HERE.
hooks.say: Your gym bag has been ready for weeks. You haven't.

hooks.label: THE BAG YOU STEP OVER
hooks.say: You step around the same gym bag every morning and promise it tomorrow.

hooks.label: IF YOUR GYM BAG COULD TALK
hooks.say: What would your gym bag say, if it could talk?

beats.say: Your gym bag has been *ready* for weeks. You haven't.
beats.scene: A packed duffel bag slumps down by a closed front door, dust drifting in a thin line of light under the door.

beats.say: Shoes packed, towel folded, bottle full. It did its *part*.
beats.scene: Close on the bag: shoes, a folded towel and a water bottle pop up out of the open zip one by one.

beats.say: And every morning, you walk around it and say *tomorrow*.
beats.scene: A wall clock above the bag spins through mornings while the light flips from day to night and back. The bag never moves.

beats.say: You're waiting for a perfect *Monday*, a perfect plan.
beats.scene: A tear-off calendar on the wall flips its pages, each one the same word, MONDAY.

beats.say: The bag's only waiting for one small *step* out that door.
beats.scene: The door swings open and warm morning light floods across the floor onto the bag.

beats.say: Send this to the friend whose bag is still by the *door*.
beats.scene: Wide shot: the open doorway glowing, the bag sitting in the light, a sign reading TODAY on the bag tag.
